subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: Which scoped inbound-media ownership model should OpenClaw support for multi-agent deployments before implementation: account, resolved agent, session/tenant, channel/chat provenance, or an explicit sharing contract?
rationale: The code path is clear, but choosing the wrong scope can either leave cross-agent leakage in place or break existing managed-media references and plugin/channel behavior.

options.title: Define one scoped managed-media contract
options.body: Use this issue as the broad design owner and implement storage, resolver, staging, cleanup, docs, and tests together.

options.title: Limit to account-scoped saves
options.body: Implement the narrower account-ID directory approach, accepting follow-up work for sessions, tenants, channel provenance, and explicit sharing.

options.title: Reject core isolation for now
options.body: Leave isolation to operator filesystem policy and close the related reports as not planned.

recommendation.title: Define one scoped managed-media contract
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the broad design owner and implement storage, resolver, staging, cleanup, docs, and tests together.

likelyOwner.reason: The core media store, managed-reference, and staging history most strongly routes through this owner trail.
